column2: [Root.GetTitledFirstName] has begun weaving spells over the battlefield. Fire, lightning and worse fall on the enemy ranks.
[Root.GetTitledFirstName] has begun casting over the battlefield, and where the Winds of Magic tear thin, daemons of the Dark Gods step through to fight at our side.
[Root.GetTitledFirstName] has spilled enough blood for the Blood God to notice. Bloodletters claw their way into the world to join the slaughter.
[Root.GetTitledFirstName] has begun calling the dead of the battlefield back to their feet. The fallen rise to fight again, on our side this time.

One of your commanders is a mage, a daemon summoner or a battle priest, and has just led troops into battle.

Battle magic is automatic. Every five days of fighting, each such commander conjures spell units for their side, and Chaos sorcerers and the Blood God's chosen may summon daemons as well. The spell units vanish when the battle ends.

Each caster can only do this a limited number of times per battle. Their magic pool depends mostly on their magic potential, and a little on their magic power. Heavy armour that is not made for casters shrinks it.
[Root.GetTitledFirstName] has begun working spells against the walls. Each month the siege lasts, the defenders will suffer more.

One of your commanders is a mage or a daemon summoner, and is besieging an enemy holding.\n\nFrom the second month of a siege, each such commander wears down the defences. The stronger their magic power (1 to 4), the harsher the damage, and it grows worse every month the siege lasts. The Blood God's summoners and the dead-raisers count as power 2. While casting against the walls, a commander has one point less in their battle magic pool for three months.
